Hi Johnathan / Sarah,

Thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap and next steps so we have alignment on the on-prem air-gapped path we discussed. High level takeaways from the call:

- You prefer a fully offline air-gapped deployment in your DR datacenter for PII workloads. Hosted API is ruled out for those workloads.
- Primary options under consideration: Private VPC (cloud but customer-managed) for non-PII workloads vs full on-prem air-gapped for sensitive models.
- Hardware questions: you want recommendations on GPU count, NVMe sizing, and whether we support GPU passthrough vs node-level inference for your existing rack design.
- Offline ops: patching windows, security reviews, and the airgap transfer process for model updates were the main follow ups.

Next steps I committed to:
1) Share the hardware requirements doc and a short checklist for air-gapped installs (attached).
2) Have Dylan (our SE) follow up with specifics on NVMe sizing and recommended GPU configs based on your 1k QPS target during peak batch windows.
3) Coordinate a 30 minute session with your infra team next week to review the network diagram and egress restrictions.

Attachments: network_diagram.pdf, hardware_requirements_v2.xlsx, airgap-deployment-checklist.docx

Proposed times for the infra review: Tue 8/4 10:00-10:30 PDT or Wed 8/5 14:00-14:30 PDT. Which works for you?

Thanks,

Marissa —

Appreciate the recap. Confirming a few data points from our side:

- Target production workload is around 800-1,200 inference QPS for short requests (avg token length ~60), with nightly batch jobs for re-indexing and retraining prep.
- We currently have 4x 4U racks available in our DR site with dual 100Gb uplinks to the staging network.
- Security: CISO wants model artifacts to be staged via encrypted USB + airgap transfer from a hardened jump box. No direct internet egress from the inference cluster.
- Maintenance: monthly maintenance window on Saturdays 02:00-05:00 local time.

We reviewed the hardware_requirements_v2.xlsx briefly and had a couple of immediate questions:
- For the NVMe recommendation you list 8TB per node. Is that per-GPU or per-node? We want to size correctly for KV cache growth.
- Any concerns about running with our existing CentOS hardened image? Our infra team prefers not to change base OS unless necessary.

We can do Tue 8/4 10:00 PDT for the infra review call. I'll invite our infra lead Mike Lee and stick to the agenda you proposed.

Thanks,

Johnathan — thanks, that timing works. A few clarifications ahead of Tue's infra call so we can come prepared:

- NVMe sizing: our typical guidance in the doc is 8TB per node assuming multi-GPU nodes with shared local cache. For KV cache heavy workloads we sometimes recommend 12-16TB per node. Dylan will propose a node sizing matrix tied to your QPS numbers.
- CentOS: our runtime supports several distros; we regularly deploy on CentOS/RHEL variants in customer air-gapped environments. We'll bring a short compatibility checklist to the call.
- Airgap model update flow: we'll walk through the encrypted package transfer via a hardened jump box and our recommended signing process for model artifacts.

Action items before Tue:
- Dylan: prepare a sizing slide with GPU counts, expected throughput, and NVMe per node variants.
- Marissa: share the hardware_requirements_v2.xlsx and network_diagram.pdf (attached).
- Johnathan: confirm Mike Lee and provide a short list of any additional security reviewers who should join.

See you Tue 8/4 10:00 PDT — calendar invite sent.

Best,
Marissa

From: Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: On-prem air-gapped deployment — hardware & offline ops follow-up

Hi all — quick technical notes ahead of tomorrow:

- NVMe: for KV cache we'd size per node rather than per GPU. For your 1k peak QPS and avg token lengths, start with 12TB/node if you want comfortable headroom for cache growth and local eval snapshots. If you expect heavy long-context jobs, bump to 16TB.
- GPUs: recommended starting point is 4x A100 80GB per node for latency SLOs under 10ms for short generation requests. If you prefer more throughput at slightly higher latency, 8x A30 in a sharded setup is an option.
- Offline ops: our airgap checklist assumes model packages are signed with customer keys and transferred via a jump box with a one-time verification step on the inference cluster. Patching can be staged into your monthly maintenance window; we support offline patch bundles that can be applied with our orchestration tool without internet.

I'll bring a short sizing deck and a one-page airgap operations runbook to the call. If there's anything else specific you'd like covered, reply and I'll add it.

Thanks,
Dylan
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
